arxiv-2204-07312.title: Structural Analysis of Branch-and-Cut and the Learnability of Gomory Mixed Integer Cuts
arxiv-2204-07312.creator: Maria-Florina Balcan, Siddharth Prasad, Tuomas Sandholm, Ellen Vitercik
arxiv-2204-07312.description: Abstract The incorporation of cutting planes within the branch-and-bound algorithm, known as branch-and-cut, forms the backbone of modern integer programming solvers. These solvers are the foremost method for solving discrete optimization problems and thus have a vast array of applications in machine learning, operations research, and many other fields.

arxiv-2209-03577.title: Peak in the critical current density in (Ca x Sr 1-x ) 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 tuned towards the structural quantum critical point
arxiv-2209-03577.creator: Xinyou Liu, Wei Zhang, Kwing To Lai, K. Moriyama, J. L. Tallon, K. Yoshimura, Swee K. Goh
arxiv-2209-03577.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xinyou Liu, Wei Zhang, Kwing To Lai, K. Moriyama, J. L. Tallon, K. Yoshimura, Swee K. Goh. (Ca x Sr 1-x ) 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 is a rare system that has been shown to display an interesting interplay between structural quantum criticality and superconductivity. A putative structural quantum critical point, which is hidden beneath a broad superconducting dome, is believed to give rise to optimized superconducting properties in (Ca x Sr 1-x ) 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 .

arxiv-2310-04122.title: VI-Diff: Unpaired Visible-Infrared Translation Diffusion Model for Single Modality Labeled Visible-Infrared Person Re-identification
arxiv-2310-04122.creator: Han Huang Yan Huang Liang Wang
arxiv-2310-04122.description: Abstract Visible-Infrared person re-identification (VI-ReID) in real-world scenarios poses a significant challenge due to the high cost of cross-modality data annotation. Different sensing cameras, such as RGB/IR cameras for good/poor lighting conditions, make it costly and error-prone to identify the same person across modalities.

arxiv-2412-11266.title: Bayesian inference of mean velocity fields and turbulence models from flow MRI
arxiv-2412-11266.creator: A. Kontogiannis, P. Nair, M. Loecher, D. B. Ennis, A. Marsden, M. P. Juniper † \dagger
arxiv-2412-11266.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by A. Kontogiannis, P. Nair, M. Loecher, D. B. Ennis, A. Marsden, M. P. Juniper † \dagger. Bayesian inference of mean velocity fields from flow MRI

We solve a Bayesian inverse Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) problem that assimilates mean flow data by jointly reconstructing the mean flow field and learning its unknown RANS parameters. We devise an algorithm that learns the most likely parameters of an algebraic effective viscosity model, and estimates their uncertainties, from mean flow data of a turbulent flow.

arxiv-2508-21485.title: Interpolation for Converse PDL
arxiv-2508-21485.creator: Johannes Kloibhofer, Valentina Trucco Dalmas, Yde Venema
arxiv-2508-21485.description: Abstract Converse 𝖯𝖣𝖫 \mathsf{PDL} is the extension of propositional dynamic logic with a converse operation on programs. Our main result states that Converse 𝖯𝖣𝖫 \mathsf{PDL} enjoys the (local) Craig Interpolation Property, with respect to both atomic programs and propositional variables. As a corollary we establish the Beth Definability Property for the logic.

arxiv-2510-01552.title: Polar: Automating Cyber Threat Prioritization through LLM-Powered Assessment
arxiv-2510-01552.creator: Luoxi Tang 1 , Yuqiao Meng 1 , Ankita Patra 1 , Weicheng Ma 2 , Muchao Ye 3 , Zhaohan Xi 1
arxiv-2510-01552.description: Abstract The rapid expansion of the cyber threat landscape, with over 11,000 new vulnerabilities reported in 2024 alone, has intensified the need for effective threat prioritization. Existing approaches, from rule-based systems to machine learning models, struggle with scalability, distribution shift, and context-independent scoring, often mis-ranking threats in dynamic exploitation environments.

pmc-13671703.title: Spatially-offset optical coherence tomography (SO-OCT) for high dynamic range biological imaging at depth
pmc-13671703.creator: Emi C V Hughes, Ralf Mouthaan, Freja Høier, Gavrielle R Untracht, Peter E Andersen, Kishan Dholakia
pmc-13671703.description: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) in highly scattering media is limited by strong backscattering from superficial layers, which reduces sensitivity to weaker signals from deeper regions. Spatially-offset OCT (SO-OCT) addresses this limitation by introducing laterally displaced illumination and detection paths, thereby preferentially sampling photons originating from increased depths.
